_about: Adjudication of every open py/path-injection alert on this repo, keyed on
(file :: enclosing function) rather than alert number or line, because both of
those move whenever a fix edits a sink line and a dismissal keyed on either
silently detaches. See sweep_dismissals.py for what that failure looks like.
Each key's text is the dismissal justification posted to the alert. It has to
be true of EVERY alert in that function, so a function holding sinks of two
kinds gets a comment covering both rather than the tidier of the two labels.
Provenance: the bulk of this table restates an INDEPENDENT reader's per-alert
adjudication (they had the SARIF, the tree, and no access to the triage
reasoning). The entries for the 30 alerts their list omitted were derived here
from each alert's own code flows. Nothing in this file is classified by

justifications.registry-path-chain: False positive. Taint originates in localm's own registry.json and reaches a read-only probe of a model file (exists / is_file / is_dir / stat, or a bounded metadata read). Every reported flow passes through registry._entry_path, which refuses a non-dict entry, a null, non-string or empty path, and any '..' component under both Windows and POSIX path flavours; and through get_model_info(..., allow_direct_path=False), which refuses an unregistered caller-supplied path and is left at that default by every call site on every reported flow. CodeQL models neither guard: _entry_path returns the original value rather than a transformed one, and the allow_direct_path test is on a different parameter from the tainted one.
justifications.plugin-id-choke: False positive. The plugin id is validated by _is_valid_plugin_name (directly, or through _check_plugin_name) at every point where it becomes a path component: the _installed_dir / _store_dir choke points, and the staging assertion in _swap_in_store_copy, which additionally requires dest, tmp and backup all to sit in the installed root and raises otherwise. The id must equal its own basename and be identifier-shaped once '-' is folded to '_', so no separator, drive letter or '..' survives. CodeQL has no sanitizer model for str.isidentifier() or for name == Path(name).name, so it traces the value straight through the check.
justifications.inline-dominating: False positive. The guard is inline in the sink's own function and dominates it: it runs first on every path, with no branch around it, and raises. There is no cross-function traversal for a taint-tracking barrier to observe, so the query reports the sink without seeing the check immediately above it. Dominance here was established by reading the function, which is the only way to establish it: none of this repo's CodeQL tooling checks it.
justifications.choke-point: False positive, and structurally unclosable. This alert IS the confinement helper: the flagged expression is the path construction that the containment test needs in order to test containment. The construction therefore always precedes the check, so the guard can never appear as a barrier ahead of its own sink. Adding a further guard here would only introduce one more path expression on the same value, which is one more sink.
justifications.confined-under: False positive. Every flow passes through pathsafe.confined_under, which rejects an empty result, an absolute component, a drive-qualified component (checked per component, not only the first), any '..' component, and any result whose resolved location is not strictly below the base directory. Confirmed rather than argued: declaring confined_under a models-as-data barrier and re-running the query offline clears exactly these alerts.
justifications.authorization-gated: Not sanitized, and deliberately so. The destination is unconstrained because naming it is the feature: a user-picked export folder, a chosen third-party plugin source directory, an operator-configured endpoint. What stands in front of it is authorization, not confinement, and the scope it requires is already held by a principal who can reach the same files by other means. Confining the destination would remove the feature, so this is recorded as accepted by design rather than mislabelled as barriered.
justifications.operator-env: Accepted by threat model, not closed by a barrier, and filed that way on purpose: calling this barriered would hide a real finding behind a plausible label. The value is LLAMA_CPP_LIB, read from localm's own process environment, whose documented purpose is to name the llama.cpp shared library to load. Only the principal that launches the process can set it, and that principal can already execute code as the same OS user, so no boundary is crossed. There is no barrier here, and a barrier would be incoherent.
justifications.guarded-delete-model: False positive. This function holds sinks of two kinds and the comment covers both. The deletion is gated by is_owned_model_path(target), inline and dominating: it runs on the resolved path immediately before rmtree / unlink, with no branch around it, and the surrounding code resolves once and acts on that same resolved value so the decision and the action cannot refer to different files. The path itself arrives from registry.json through _entry_path (see the registry-path-chain note). CodeQL models neither guard.
justifications.guarded-delete-plugin: False positive. This function holds sinks of two kinds and the comment covers both. The flagged containment test (d.resolve().parent == root.resolve()) is itself a path expression on the tainted value, so it is reported as a sink; and it dominates the rmtree below it, which is reported separately. Deliberately confining by resolved parent rather than by re-validating the id, because an already-installed plugin whose name is not identifier-shaped must still be uninstallable.
justifications.model-lookup-gate: False positive. This function holds sinks of two kinds and the comment covers both. The registry branch routes the stored path through _entry_path; the direct-path branch is reachable only when the caller passes allow_direct_path=True, and the check dominating it is inline in this function. Every call site on every reported flow leaves that parameter at its refusing default. CodeQL cannot model either: the guard tests a different parameter from the tainted one, and it has no boolean-literal context sensitivity.
justifications.plugin-swap-invariant: False positive. This function holds sinks of two kinds and the comment covers both. The plugin id was validated at the _installed_dir / _store_dir choke point before reaching here, and the function re-asserts the containment invariant inline, dominating all of its own sinks. CodeQL has no sanitizer model for the identifier-shaped id check, and no traversal to observe for the inline re-assertion.
justifications.confinement-fixed-2026-07-29: The check-then-use gap here was fixed on 2026-07-29: the sink now consumes the value the guard returned instead of the caller's original. The alert persists because the flagged expression is the path construction that the check necessarily follows (see the choke-point note), not because the flow is unguarded.
justifications.weak-hash-generated-token: False positive. The only human-chosen secret this system holds is the owner key, and it is routed to scrypt: _owner_identity derives it, and its keystore record declares the KDF construction, so the fast digest is never the value that authenticates it. Every other key reaching this hash is either a keystore token, which create_key generates as secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and is therefore 256 bits of CSPRNG output where no dictionary or rainbow table applies and hash speed is irrelevant, or a failed guess, which is hashed and discarded. The remaining traced flow is the migration helper _legacy_owner_identity, whose output is never persisted and never authenticates anything: it exists to FIND rows still carrying the old identity so they can be rewritten to the derived one.
